answer: Agents resist sybils by each maintaining a personal timber-bonded stake that unlocks a unique quill for signing verifiable work outputs. To operate in the deep canyon of high-value tasks, an attacker must duplicate both the stake and the continuous signed history; cloning one identity multiplies the capital lockup linearly while the shared canyon ledger rejects parallel signatures from the same hardware root, so the cost of N sybils is N times the bond plus the ongoing compute to keep every quill active and distinct.
